primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators IV
primary_antecedent.scope: Independent full one-dimensional descent, including radial curves, entire collapsed fibers, exact tensor indices and closed-interval concavity.

source_correspondence: Full Theorem 26.9.4 is proved with the actual indefinite endpoint hypothesis, every real operator order, complete compact fibers and closed-interval extended concavity.
The intrinsic transverse form and its exact nonnegative scalar define the quotient. Compact fiber infima give lower semicontinuity and finite local negative-Sobolev bounds.
Radial characteristics are handled directly by conicity of the exact indices and the elementary minimum-with-a-constant concavity inequality.

For each nonradial zero fiber, cosphere regularity and injectivity are proved by flow uniqueness. Opposite tangent returns are impossible; a closed zero-Hessian projected orbit contradicts the nearby indefinite points. A whole-fiber homogeneous tube has indefinite endpoints inside the original interval.
Exact graph inverses and elliptic order reducers retain the complete operator and give the all-real m-minus-one source shift on the whole fiber.

The constant-variable lemma proves both Sobolev membership implications at every real order. The reverse direction integrates over a bounded extra-frequency interval with positive Fourier mass. Endpoint membership is not inferred from an index.
The ordinary tensor wavefront identity is proved with one fixed cone for all decay orders, independently of the potentially weaker infinite-index assertion.
The extra angular cutoff gives a genuine classical symbol in all frequencies. Its principal symbol satisfies condition P and has a nonzero temporal differential.

The localized tensor equation is justified on compactly supported inputs. The angular-complement error is rapidly decreasing in the extra frequency; proper-kernel and base-localization errors are smooth.

The actual lifted characteristic surface, its compact zero fibers and its reduced complex strip are identified exactly. The new defining differential remains nonzero even when the original transverse differential vanishes.
The full two-dimensional propagation theorem applies with exactly the original source and unknown fiber indices. Superharmonicity independent of the imaginary coordinate gives local affine concavity.
Finite truncation, uniform mesh interpolation, nonincreasing chord slopes and monotone limits give global interior concavity. Endpoint lower semicontinuity proves the full closed-interval conclusion.
The factorized extension is stated with its actual exact hypotheses.
Three complete solutions give the sharp delta threshold, a smooth flat collapsed strip and a radial indefinite curve. The original figure uses exact formulas and no numerical integration.

programme_proofs.proof_locator: **G0. Radial curves already have the required concavity.**
**G1. Each nonradial collapsed fiber has an embedded cosphere projection.**
**G2. The exact homogeneous model and the source shift.**
**T0. Define the extension and prove both Sobolev inequalities.**
**T1. The ordinary wavefront set and locality.**
**L1. The equation retains the exact source index.**
**L2. Identify the actual leaf and the collapsed fibers.**
**C0. Apply the full propagation theorem on each quotient neighborhood.**
**C1. Local concavity, extended values and endpoints.**

source_result_coverage.source_result_and_exact_scope: Exact factorized extension stated after Theorem 26.9.4

component_scope: A characteristic curve can contain a whole interval on which its transverse quadratic form vanishes. The correct regularity statement collapses that interval before testing concavity. We prove the statement by adding one real variable, applying the two-dimensional propagation theorem, and returning to the original curve. The auxiliary variable changes neither the distribution's microlocal Sobolev index nor its source index.
